title: cost-optimization-autotune-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Ava Chen
description:
Context: Our autotune system previously exposed knobs for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization but required manual tuning and per-customer experimentation. This PR implements a set of production-safe defaults, an autotune flow that learns from traffic, and first-class unit-economics (uecon) tooling in the Console to estimate cost/latency trade-offs.

Summary of changes: Updated runtime defaults for batching/windowing and caching TTLs, introduced a pluggable quantization profile loader and selector, added an offline autotune worker that emits candidate config diffs, and shipped a Console pane that visualizes expected token costs and latency impact for each candidate. The changes are intended to reduce average per-token cost while maintaining latency SLOs for common production workloads.

What changed (high level):
- Redwood runtime: default batching window reduced from 20ms to 12ms when QPS < 50 to reduce latency tail. Continuous batching algorithm now includes a traffic-aware upper bound and priority for pinned low-latency routes.
- KV/prefix cache: default cache TTLs and allowed prefixes updated; introduced adaptive TTL that short-circuits caching for high-entropy routes (e.g. chat with many user-specific tokens).
- Quantization: added quant/profiles.yaml schema and a runtime selector that picks compatible q8_0/q4_0 variants based on model, hardware, and the autotune score. Profiles include safe-fallbacks for GPUs without INT8 support.
- Autotune worker: background task (optimize/autotune/service.go) that analyzes request traces, simulates candidate configs using historical traces, scores them by uecon delta and latency tail penalty, and emits proposals to the control plane.
- Console (uecon tooling): new UI pane and API endpoints to preview unit-econ estimates, simulate cost/latency for candidate configs, and accept/reject rollout proposals. Includes CSV export for finance reviews.
- Tests/benchmarks: added an end-to-end harness that runs sampled traces through the simulation pipeline and verifies no >5% latency-SLO regressions for accepted proposals.

Commits (summary):
- feat(runtime): adaptive batching and traffic-aware upper bound
- feat(cache): adaptive TTL and safe prefix heuristics
- feat(quant): add quant profiles schema and selection logic
- feat(autotune): offline worker + scoring pipeline
- feat(console): uecon preview pane + API
- test(bench): e2e simulation harness + sample traces
- ci: add integration job to run simulation on PR changes

Files changed (high level):
- redwood/runtime/batching.go
- redwood/runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.go
- redwood/runtime/cache/config.go
- redwood/quant/profiles.yaml
- redwood/optimize/autotune/service.go
- redwood/optimize/autotune/simulator.go
- redwood-console/src/components/uecon/PreviewPane.tsx
- redwood-console/api/uecon_preview.go
- redwood-cli/bin/uecon-sim (small helper)
- tests/bench/e2e_simulation_test.go

Testing and CI: CI initially flagged integration tests that validate simulation accuracy (some flakiness due to trace sampling). I re-ran the integration job after tightening the deterministic seed and increasing the sample size for low-qps traces. Final CI run: build: passed, unit tests: passed, integration (simulation): passed after rerun, linter: passed. ci_status is set to pass.

Review notes & discussion (selected):
- Priya Singh: "Can we guarantee there are no customer-visible regression windows during rollout? Suggest adding a canary rollout path that pins a small percentage of traffic and auto-rolls back on >3% latency SLO violation."
- Author (Ava): "Agreed. Added rollout policy hooks in control plane; default proposals are canary-by-default (5%) and require manual opt-in for 100% rollout. Documented in release notes." 
- Diego Martinez: "Quant profile selection is clever, but please ensure we have telemetry when we fall back to non-quantized variants. We need observability to debug quality regressions." 
- Author (Ava): "Added telemetry: quant_profile_applied metric + fallback_reason tag. Also created dashboard tiles in perf-canary repo referencing these metrics."
- Ethan Park: "Simulation harness is heavy; can we run a lightweight approximation in the hot path to keep proposal latency low?" 
- Author (Ava): "Autotune worker remains offline for heavy sims. We added a fast estimator for quick proposals; heavy sims run asynchronously and emit confidence scores. See optimize/autotune/estimator.go for details."

Acceptance criteria and rollout plan: Proposals are created by the offline worker and visible in Console. Default policy is canary at 5% QPS for 24h, requiring no more than 3% increase in p99 latency and a positive uecon delta (cost reduced by at least 2%). Ops can accept/reject and schedule rollouts. We also added a scheduled nightly job to re-evaluate accepted configs and auto-recover if traffic patterns change.

Backward compatibility and safety: All defaults are opt-in for Dedicated and Private clusters via config flags. Hosted API receives opt-out indicators for customers under strict SLA. Quantization profiles include safe fallbacks, and the runtime will only apply profiles marked as "production_safe" in profiles.yaml. No breaking API changes.

Migration notes: Operators upgrading private/dedicated clusters should run the provided simulation tool (redwood-cli uecon-sim) against recent traces before enabling autotune. For most customers the defaults provide immediate ~6-12% unit-cost savings in internal benchmarks.

Release notes: "Introduce autotune defaults for batching and caching, quantization profile support, and Console unit-economics tooling. Adds offline simulation and canary rollout controls. Expected to reduce per-token cost by 6-12% for typical workloads while preserving latency SLOs."

Merge outcome: Squash-and-merge after approvals from Priya and Diego and green CI. The PR includes a post-merge migration checklist in the description.
